headline: St. Lucie Mets rally past Jupiter 6-5 on Yovanny Rodriguez walk-off single
teaser: Yovanny Rodriguez delivered a two-run walk-off single in the ninth inning Wednesday as the St. Lucie Mets rallied from four runs down to beat the Jupiter Hammerheads 6-5 at Clover Park.
body:
Yovanny Rodriguez delivered a two-run walk-off single in the bottom of the ninth inning Wednesday as the St. Lucie Mets rallied from a four-run deficit to beat the Jupiter Hammerheads 6-5 at Clover Park.

The victory was the Mets' third straight and marked the first time this season St. Lucie won a game after trailing through eight innings. Jupiter dropped its seventh consecutive game.

St. Lucie entered the ninth trailing 5-4. Boston Baro, Julio Zayas and Jack Toomey each drew one-out walks to load the bases for Rodriguez. Facing Jonathan Rosario, Rodriguez hit a broken-bat ground ball that slipped past second baseman Yoffry Solano and into the outfield, allowing Baro and Zayas to score the tying and winning runs.

It was the Mets' second comeback victory in as many nights. St. Lucie trailed 6-3 at the seventh-inning stretch Tuesday before rallying to win. On Wednesday, the Mets faced an even larger deficit, trailing 5-1 entering the bottom of the seventh.

Jeremy Rodriguez started the comeback by scoring from third on a throwing error by Jupiter pitcher Ian Medina in the seventh inning. The Mets pulled within one run in the eighth when Vladi Gomez hit an RBI infield single and another run scored on a throwing error by Luis Arana, cutting Jupiter's lead to 5-4.

St. Lucie's bullpen kept the game within reach. Ernesto Mercedes, Cesar Rivera, Zach Crotchfelt and Caden Wooster combined for 4.2 scoreless innings, allowing only two hits while recording six strikeouts without issuing a walk.

Mercedes worked 1.2 perfect innings, while Crotchfelt retired the side in order in the eighth on nine pitches. Wooster pitched a scoreless ninth and earned his first victory of the season.

Mets starter Ethan Lanthier allowed five runs on six hits over 4.1 innings. He walked two and struck out four.

Jupiter outhit St. Lucie for the second consecutive night, but the Hammerheads struggled with command, issuing 12 walks overall and eight over the final three innings.

Gomez went 2-for-4 for the Mets' only multi-hit performance. Branny De Oleo reached base in all four of his plate appearances, collecting an RBI double and drawing three walks.

Jupiter first baseman Echedry Vargas went 2-for-3 with a home run and three RBIs. His two-run homer off Lanthier in the fifth inning was his Florida State League-leading 27th home run of the season.

The Mets improved to 23-38 in the second half and 56-71 overall. Jupiter fell to 24-35 in the second half and 60-65 overall.

St. Lucie and Jupiter continue their series Thursday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 6:10 p.m. The game will feature the final $2 Night promotion of the season, with select beer, hot dogs, fountain soda and popcorn available for $2.
